system.system_guide.txt:
[4m[35mSYSTEM GUIDE[0m
All the notes you need to know to navigate through the terminal.

[4m[35mNAVIGATING[0m
To go around the terminal, you need to know where you are. To do this, use [38;5;117mdir[0m or [38;5;117mls[0m.
To move around, use [38;5;117mcd[0m to change directories.
To open files, use [38;5;117mcat [filename.exe][0m to open .txt files. For .exe, .lzl, .jsn files, use [38;5;117mrun [filename.exe][0m or [38;5;117mopen[filename.exe][0m.

[4m[35mINTERACTING[0m
To make a file in your current directory, use [38;5;117mtouch [filename.exe][0m. Your file name must contain a valid extension such as: .exe, .txt, .lzl, .jsn.
To create a new directory, use [38;5;117mmkdir [dirname][0m.
To write to a file, use [38;5;117mwrite [filename.exe][0m.
To rename a file, use [38;5;117mren [filename.exe] [newname.exe][0m or [38;5;117mrename [filename.exe] [newname.exe][0m. Note that you cannot change the file extension when renaming.
To move a file, use [38;5;117mmv [filename.exe] [path][0m. Note that the new location must be a path [38;5;117m(@main/newlocation)[0m.
To delete a file, use [38;5;117mrm [filename.exe][0m.
To delete a directory, use [38;5;117mrmdir [dirname][0m.

[4m[35mHAVING FUN[0m
To repeat whatever you said, use [38;5;117mecho [message][0m. This message can be whatever you want.
To piss off the [41mOVERLORD[0m, use [38;5;117msecret(s)[0m.

[4m[35mFREE SECRETS[0m
[38;5;117mily[0m or [38;5;117mi love you[0m or...

That is all! For more secrets, figure them out! Test some stuff.
system.creator_notes.txt:
I created this project as a 'thank you' for everything you've done for me. Thank you for sticking by my side even when there was no reason to. Thank you for loving me when I found it hard to love myself. Thank you for leading by example whenever I was lost. Thank you for educating me rather than punishing me when I didn't know. You've done so much for me, [38;5;117mLezzell[0m. For all that you've done for me, I ought to present to you a project that I hope is worth at least five minutes of your time.

Every line of code is made to build a mini-terminal with secrets hidden, love to be shared, and software to be interacted with.

The commands in this are exactly what are in real terminals, with the exception of some being from multiple terminals (Windows: dir or MacOS: ls). These don't make any changes, so don't worry, it's easy to navigate.

To get more help, use the 'help' command or open 'system_guide.txt' for more insight and maybe even some [38;5;212msecrets[0m!

terminal.keys.txt:
[4m[35mABOUT THE KEYS[0m

If you type the command 'keys' or 'key', you get shown these three keys: [35mtmy[0m, [35mjsn[0m, [35mlzl[0m. As you can tell, these keys are named after things you know very well.

Originally, these keys weren't suppsoed to be anything. However, since this project has been kept up way past Lezzell's birthday, the developer decided to give them a purpose.

You must find these keys by completing certain tasks. Each key unlocks different parts of the terminal and reveal more information.

To use these keys or find out how to get them, simply type one of them in the terminal. If you really want to, you can find all of them!

inner-shell.command-line.txt:
[35mThe TCL (Termy's Command Line)[0m

Inside of this terminal (Termy), there is an inner-shell that hides under the functions of Termy.

This may sound a bit confusing, but TCL is the nucleus of the terminal.

Inside of the TCL, you may find some cool information that you really wouldn't find in this terminal. If you wish to interact with it, simply type [35mtcl[0m to get some extra information.

c-drive.information.txt:
[35mThis is your C-Drive[0m

In computers, a C-Drive is typically the main drive that stores the computers most valuable information. In this case, the terminal runs based off this drive. You may want to remove it out of curiosity, but unless you're admin, you cannot remove this drive.

This drive stores system internals, current logs, and files that make the system run.
c-drive.the-power-bank.txt:
[4m[35mABOUT THE POWER BANK[0m

Because this is a fake terminal, the C-Drive doesn't need a REAL thing to keep it running.

Well, actually, we need something. For fun, I made this run on a picture of Snoopy. Why not?

Check it out!

d-drive.information.txt:
[35mThis is your D-Drive[0m

In computers, a D-Drive is typically the secondary drive that stores personal data, backup information, and saved data.

This is your second most important drive. Any attempt to remove it will crash the terminal and reset itself.
